subject: Clarify T&C: termination for convenience, notice timing & data handoff
messages:
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>
To: Tim Browne <tim.browne@acme.com>, Acme Procurement <procurement@acme.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 16 May 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Clarify T&C: termination for convenience, notice timing & data handoff

Tim / team —

Thanks for the quick review yesterday. Attached are the latest redlines for the MSA and Order Form (MSA_redline_v3.pdf; OrderForm_Acme_v2.docx). Before we escalate to signature we need to align on three operational points that will affect onboarding cadence and any ramp credits:  

1) Termination for convenience window: Redwood typically offers a 60-day mutual termination window for order-level convenience exits; our legal team redlined the MSA to reflect that.
2) Data handoff & export: customers receive a 30-day data export window after termination; we want to confirm this meets Acme's requirements or if you need longer retention/hand-holding.
3) Service continuity & SLA impact: if termination is initiated during a committed period, we may need a short transition support fee (covers orderly KV export, runbook handoff, and final logs delivery).

Can you confirm whether Acme is comfortable with 60 days, or if you require an extended notice (and the business rationale)? If you prefer longer, we can propose a compromise language (e.g., 75 days) and a transitional support clause to minimize operational risk.

Next steps I propose: if Tim confirms timing this week, Redwood legal (Laura) will prepare a final clause and we can push to DocuSign. If you want to escalate to your procurement/legal, happy to set a 30-min sync.

Attachments: MSA_redline_v3.pdf, OrderForm_Acme_v2.docx

Best,

Hannah Schmitt
Senior Director, Sales Operations
Redwood Inference
(h) 415-555-0182 | (m) 415-555-0199

---
Note: Redwood standard wording (redline) highlighted changes to Section 9.2 (Termination for Convenience) and Section 12.4 (Data Export).

From: Tim Browne <tim.browne@acme.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>, Acme Procurement <procurement@acme.com>
Cc: Sally Wu <sally.wu@acme.com>
Date: Mon, 17 May 2027 11:04:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Clarify T&C: termination for convenience, notice timing & data handoff

Hannah —

Thanks for sending the redlines. A couple quick things from Acme legal/procurement perspective:  

- 60 days is shorter than our standard for platform contracts. Our baseline is 90 days for termination for convenience on production services; the rationale is to give our ops teams time to backfill and validate exports across regions.
- On data export: 30 days is tight for a multi-region migration. We typically request 90 days, or a contractual commitment that Redwood will retain a backup snapshot for 90 days and make exports available on request.
- Transition support fee: we are open to a fee, but prefer it to be capped and defined (example: not to exceed 10% of the monthly committed spend and only once per termination event).

If Redwood can meet us at 75 days for termination + 90 days for data export (with the capped one-time transition fee), we can likely accept and avoid further redlines. If not, we will push for 90/90 and a stronger exit acceptance clause.

Tim
Tim Browne
Senior Counsel, Contracts & Procurement
Acme Corp
(t) 212-555-6622

Date: Mon, 17 May 2027 14:26:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Clarify T&C: termination for convenience, notice timing & data handoff

Tim —

Appreciate the openness on tradeoffs. Quick commercial context from our side so you have the full picture:  

- Typical ramp: most customers are live in 4–8 weeks from signature. A longer notice increases the risk of customers holding us to committed discounts through an extended offboarding window.
- Operational cost: a 90-day export window means longer retention (storage + support) that we price into enterprise deals. To avoid surprises we propose: 75 days mutual termination + 90 days data export retention, with a one-time transition support fee capped at 8% of monthly committed spend (applies only if termination occurs before the initial 12-month commit completes).

If Acme accepts 75/90 + capped 8% fee (one-time), we can remove the redline friction and finalize the order form quickly. If you need explicit language, Laura (cc'd) can provide the clause text that limits the fee to a single occurrence and ties retention to the account's export window.

If helpful, happy to jump on a 20-min call today to close this.

Thanks,
Karthik Iyer
Head of GTM Contracts
Redwood Inference

Date: Tue, 18 May 2027 14:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Clarify T&C: termination for convenience, notice timing & data handoff

Tim —

Thanks — appreciate the clear asks. Per Karthik's commercial proposal, Redwood can accept the following compromise:  

- Termination for convenience: mutual 75-day notice period.
- Data export & retention: Redwood will retain a backup snapshot for 90 days post-termination and provide exports on request within that window.
- Transition support fee: one-time fee capped at 8% of the monthly committed spend; only payable if termination occurs within the first 12 months of the Order Form.

Suggested MSA phrasing (high-level, to be inserted into Section 9.2 and 12.4):
"On termination for convenience by either party, the parties shall provide a 75-day written notice. Redwood will make available account exports and a backup snapshot for a 90-day period following termination; Redwood's one-time transition support fee (if applicable) shall not exceed 8% of the monthly committed spend and is payable only once per Order Form if termination occurs during the first 12 months of the term."

If Acme confirms acceptance we will incorporate this text into MSA_redline_v3.pdf and send a DocuSign package (link attached) for signature. If you want slightly different triggering language for the fee (e.g., termination "during the committed period" rather than "first 12 months"), let us know; we can adjust quickly.

Laura Bennett
Counsel, Commercial Contracts
Redwood Inference
(o) 415-555-7010
